info.description:
The Tenant API gives programmatic access to your Amperity tenant through RESTful endpoints for integrations, applications, and custom workflows.

Every request must include an access token. To create an API key, generate an access token, and find your tenant ID, see [How to authenticate with Amperity APIs](https://docs.amperity.com/api/authentication.html).

**Rate limit.** The Tenant API accepts up to 10 requests per second. Requests over the limit may return HTTP 429. Response times vary by endpoint and by how much data a response returns, and some requests take seconds.

**Errors and retries.** A 4xx or 5xx response has a body with `status`, a human-readable `message`, and, when available, a `request_id` and `trace_id` to give Amperity Support. Retry a 429, 500, or 503 with exponential backoff and some randomness, so that retries do not arrive together. Do not retry other 4xx responses without changing the request.

**Sandboxes.** A sandbox uses the same base URL as production. Send its tenant ID in the `Amperity-Tenant` header.

**Changes.** See the [changelog](https://docs.amperity.com/api/changelog.html) for new versions and deprecations.
info.title: Tenant API

get.description: Return a list of draft campaigns from your tenant. You may restrict the list of draft campaigns to those associated with a specific data template.

parameters.description: Your tenant ID. For a request to a sandbox, use the sandbox's tenant ID; the base URL stays the same as production. On Microsoft Azure the tenant ID must also be in the base URL.
parameters.name: Amperity-Tenant

parameters.description: The version of the Tenant API to use, as a date such as `2024-04-01`. All endpoints are versioned together, and a new version is released only for a breaking change, such as removing or renaming an endpoint, field, header, or parameter, adding a required one, or changing a data type. Each version is supported for at least one year. Amperity gives at least 6 months' notice before a version stops being supported, using the `Deprecation` and `Sunset` response headers; a request that names an unsupported version returns 400. `unstable` names endpoints that are still in development, with no guarantee of support, notice of changes, or availability.
parameters.name: Api-Version

parameters.description: A supported version of the Tenant API. You may use the `api-version` request header instead of the `api-version` request parameter.
parameters.name: api_version

parameters.description: Set this value to `true` to include a total count of all results. Default value: `false`. Obtaining the total count of all results can be an expensive operation when there is a high number of pages in the results set.
parameters.name: with_total

parameters.description: The maximum number of records to include in a single page of results.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: An opaque token that is used to paginate results. Omit the `next_token` property to return the first page. Use the cursor value for `next_token` that was returned in a response to view the next page of results.
parameters.name: next_token

parameters.description: Use this parameter to restrict the list of campaigns that are returned to only campaigns that are configured to use specific data template.
parameters.name: destination_data_template_id

404.description: Not found: the resource does not exist.

405.description: Method not allowed: the endpoint does not support this HTTP method.

500.description: Internal error. Simplify the request, or retry with exponential backoff.
